scenes.visual: Title card: The Choice Becomes an Address.

scenes.tts: A neuron has chosen its receptor. How does its axon know where to go?
scenes.visual: Olfactory neurons in the nose, each a different colour, send axons toward the olfactory bulb. Question mark at the bulb.
scenes.narration: A neuron has chosen its receptor. How does its axon know where to go?

scenes.tts: The core rule is one receptor and two glomeruli. That needs each neuron's axon to find the right target.
scenes.visual: Axons of one colour converge on two matching glomeruli in the bulb.
scenes.narration: The core rule is one receptor and two glomeruli. That needs each neuron's axon to find the right target.

scenes.tts: In nineteen ninety-six, Mombaerts and colleagues swapped receptor genes in mice.
scenes.caption: In 1996, Mombaerts and colleagues swapped receptor genes in mice.
scenes.visual: One receptor gene is cut out and another put in its place. Label: Mombaerts and colleagues, 1996.
scenes.narration: In 1996, Mombaerts and colleagues swapped receptor genes in mice.

scenes.tts: The results suggested that receptor identity is instructive in axon targeting, but not the only factor.
scenes.visual: The swapped axons shift toward a new target but do not land exactly on it. Label: instructive, not exclusive.
scenes.narration: The results suggested that receptor identity is instructive in axon targeting, but not the only factor.

scenes.tts: So the receptor is one input among several.
scenes.visual: The receptor icon joins other, unlabelled guidance inputs at the axon tip.
scenes.narration: So the receptor is one input among several.

scenes.tts: If the receptor helps choose the target, how could it change what the growing axon carries?
scenes.visual: A neuron with a receptor and a nucleus, an axon tip far away, linked by a dotted question mark.
scenes.narration: If the receptor helps choose the target, how could it change what the growing axon carries?

scenes.tts: One route runs through cyclic A M P. Imai and colleagues reported receptor-derived cyclic A M P signals shift guidance molecule expression.
scenes.caption: One route runs through cAMP. Imai and colleagues reported receptor-derived cAMP signals shift guidance molecule expression.
scenes.visual: Inside the neuron, a cAMP signal raises some guidance-molecule genes in the nucleus; their proteins then appear on the growing axon. Label: Imai and colleagues, 2006.
scenes.narration: One route runs through cAMP. Imai and colleagues reported receptor-derived cAMP signals shift guidance molecule expression.

scenes.tts: It also shifts where axons project in the bulb, along the front-to-back axis.
scenes.visual: Axon endpoints slide along the anterior-posterior axis of the bulb as the cAMP level changes.
scenes.narration: It also shifts where axons project in the bulb, along the front-to-back axis.

scenes.tts: Serizawa and colleagues found four adhesion and guidance molecules whose levels vary with receptor activity.
scenes.visual: Label: Serizawa and colleagues, 2006. Names on screen: Kirrel2, Kirrel3, ephrin-A5, EphA5. Bars for each rise and fall as a receptor-activity dial turns.
scenes.narration: Serizawa and colleagues found four adhesion and guidance molecules whose levels vary with receptor activity.

scenes.tts: How such molecules build the map is covered in the lesson on topographic maps.
scenes.visual: A pointer to the topographic maps lesson.
scenes.narration: How such molecules build the map is covered in the lesson on topographic maps.

scenes.tts: Now recall the lock. Its relay ran through the kinase Perk.
scenes.caption: Now recall the lock. Its relay ran through the kinase PERK.
scenes.visual: The lock chain from chapter 4, with PERK highlighted.
scenes.narration: Now recall the lock. Its relay ran through the kinase PERK.

scenes.tts: The lock's own pathway reaches the wiring too.
scenes.visual: A branch grows from PERK toward a set of guidance genes.
scenes.narration: The lock's own pathway reaches the wiring too.

scenes.tts: Shayya and colleagues reported that different receptor sequences produce different patterns of stress in developing neurons.
scenes.visual: Several neurons, each with a different receptor, show endoplasmic reticulum stress meters at different levels. Label: Shayya and colleagues, 2022.
scenes.narration: Shayya and colleagues reported that different receptor sequences produce different patterns of stress in developing neurons.

scenes.tts: A gene called D D I T three links Perk signalling to guidance and adhesion genes.
scenes.caption: A gene called Ddit3 links PERK signalling to guidance and adhesion genes.
scenes.visual: Ddit3 sits between PERK and a cluster of guidance and adhesion genes.
scenes.narration: A gene called Ddit3 links PERK signalling to guidance and adhesion genes.

scenes.tts: So the stress signal that helps hold the choice can also influence where the axon goes.
scenes.visual: One arrow from PERK splits: one branch to the lock, one to the axon tip.
scenes.narration: So the stress signal that helps hold the choice can also influence where the axon goes.

scenes.tts: These are mouse reports. They show a link, not the full rules for building the map.
scenes.visual: Caveat card: mouse; a link, not the full wiring rules.
scenes.narration: These are mouse reports. They show a link, not the full rules for building the map.

scenes.tts: The choice and the address can share a signal. Choosing a receptor helps set where the axon goes.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: one signal, two jobs: hold the choice, tune the address.
scenes.narration: The choice and the address can share a signal. Choosing a receptor helps set where the axon goes.

scenes.visual: End card: The Choice Becomes an Address.
